stories.body: Russian missiles struck Kyiv overnight, wounding six people and sending residents to shelters, Ukrainian authorities said. The attack came as the Kremlin said it was ready to resume US-mediated trilateral talks with Ukraine next month following Vladimir Putin's meeting with US envoy Steve Witkoff. Donald Trump said negotiations were closer than ever to ending the war, while Moscow voiced doubts about Ukrainian and European proposals.
stories.headline: Russia signals readiness for new US-Ukraine talks after Kyiv missile strike

stories.body: The US State Department ordered some diplomats and family members to leave Saudi Arabia amid near-daily Houthi attacks on airports and energy infrastructure. Saudi authorities reported deaths and injuries after attacks on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam and an intercepted drone near the Shaybah oilfield. The State Department said reports of wider withdrawals from other Gulf countries were inaccurate, although officials told Reuters that plans for further family departures were under consideration.
stories.headline: Houthi attacks prompt US diplomatic departures from Saudi Arabia

stories.body: French authorities banned demonstrations near key Paris sites as they prepared for further unrest after violent protests and looting over the cost of living. President Emmanuel Macron accused foreign leaders, including Donald Trump, of exploiting the violence for political purposes and spreading misleading narratives, including AI-generated images. The unrest has prompted travel warnings and pushed French 10-year government bond yields above 5%, their highest level since 2002.
stories.headline: France bans protests after violent unrest as Macron criticizes foreign leaders

stories.body: The UN Environment Programme says national commitments to reduce emissions remain far below what is needed to meet the Paris Agreement's 1.5°C goal. On current commitments, the world is heading toward about 2.6°C of warming this century, sharpening the challenge for leaders ahead of the COP31 climate summit in Turkey.
stories.headline: UN warns the world is on course to breach the 1.5°C warming limit

stories.body: A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion after a jury found that the company had deceived users about its data-privacy practices in a case connected to the Cambridge Analytica scandal. The judge imposed the maximum state penalty of $5,000 for each violation and said interest would accrue at 15% annually until payment. Meta has called the penalty a tax on speech and has previously settled related privacy claims elsewhere in the US.
stories.headline: Meta ordered to pay $25 billion in New Mexico privacy case

stories.body: Republicans have spent substantially more than Democrats on broadcast advertising in key Senate states, but much of that money comes from outside groups that pay higher rates than candidates and political parties. In Ohio, Texas and Michigan, the resulting share of ads on air is far closer than the spending totals suggest. Democratic candidates' fundraising and lower ad rates have helped offset Republican super-PAC spending, while Republican groups have invested heavily in mail, calls and texts.
stories.headline: Republican TV spending advantage is weakened by reliance on outside groups

stories.body: Georgia Republicans see wealthy first-time candidate Rick Jackson as their best chance to protect the party from broader losses, even as Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff maintains an advantage over Republican Mike Collins. Jackson has spent nearly $200 million in the governor's race and has sought to emphasize his association with Governor Brian Kemp rather than Donald Trump. Party strategists worry that Trump's visits could energize Democratic voters, while Jackson needs both crossover voters and the Republican base to win.
stories.headline: Georgia Republicans look to Rick Jackson to contain a potential midterm wipeout

stories.body: New York Democratic congressional candidate Brad Lander was among about 80 American, Israeli and British volunteers detained by Israeli security forces while helping Palestinians harvest olives near Nahalin in the occupied West Bank. Organizers said the group was peacefully harvesting on private Palestinian land when the military declared the area a closed zone. Israeli officials said the harvest had not been coordinated in advance and described the large group as provocative; Lander was released after receiving a warning.
stories.headline: Brad Lander detained while joining West Bank olive harvest

stories.body: Spain's Constitutional Court declined to hear an appeal seeking to restore voting rights for roughly 160,000 citizens naturalized under the Democratic Memory Law before the November 29 general election. The court said the appeal was premature because the Supreme Court's suspension of their voting rights is not final. The dispute concerns people granted nationality under a government instruction on descendants of exiles, which Vox and Iustitia Europa have challenged.
stories.headline: Court leaves voting rights of 160,000 naturalized Spaniards unresolved

stories.body: Argentine President Javier Milei's visit to Madrid has become a campaign issue ahead of Spain's November general election. Milei insulted Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and praised Santiago Abascal, while Sánchez linked Milei, Abascal and PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo to austerity and cuts. Madrid mayor José Luis Martínez-Almeida, of the PP, acknowledged that the visit offered Sánchez useful political ammunition.
stories.headline: Javier Milei's Madrid visit becomes a flashpoint in Spain's election campaign

stories.body: More than 100 migrants who entered Ceuta during a mass crossing at the end of July have received international protection, allowing them to remain, live and work legally in Spain. Authorities have issued 180 asylum decisions since July 31, although some concerned people who were already in the city rather than those who arrived during the crossing.
stories.headline: More than 100 migrants who entered Ceuta in July receive asylum

stories.body: Six months after the PP formed a new round of regional governments with Vox in Extremadura, Aragón, Castilla y León and Andalucía, Vox-backed policies are advancing through regional measures and budgets. The agenda includes provisions tied to Spanish nationality in Aragón's housing law and censorship measures in Castilla y León, as PP and Vox could be approaching a national governing majority ahead of the general election.
stories.headline: PP-Vox regional coalitions advance a shared hard-right agenda

stories.body: Barcelona is preparing a proposal for a phased reopening of parts of Collserola Natural Park after months of restrictions linked to African swine fever. The city wants the Carretera de les Aigües to be among the first areas reopened, subject to technical and scientific criteria set by the Generalitat. Officials stress that reopening must be gradual to avoid renewed restrictions and protect the agricultural sector from severe economic consequences.
stories.headline: Barcelona prepares phased reopening of Collserola after swine-fever restrictions

stories.body: TMB bus workers called off planned strike days after management and unions reached a preliminary four-year collective agreement. The deal provides additional rest days, more weekend time off and a progressive reduction of the working week to 35 hours. It also cancels five further October protest days that had been scheduled after earlier negotiations failed.
stories.headline: TMB bus strike called off after management and unions reach preliminary deal

stories.body: Barcelona's ombudsman, David Bondia, has proposed exploring a collaborative purchase of the Bloc Papallona in Nova Esquerra de l'Eixample to prevent residents from being displaced. Options include purchase by housing-sector organizations and inclusion in the social-rental pool. Bondia argued that secure housing underpins other social rights and called for urgent property valuations and continued dialogue among residents, owners, social groups and the city.
stories.headline: Barcelona weighs collaborative purchase to preserve homes in the Bloc Papallona

stories.body: Mayor Jaume Collboni called for a debate on regulating commercial rents, particularly sharp increases when leases are renewed that can displace traditional neighborhood businesses. Barcelona Oberta, representing 24 shopping districts, rejected the idea as excessive intervention and instead called for easier access, more flexible land-use rules, faster administration and Sunday opening. Both sides agreed that local commerce is central to neighborhood life, though they differ on how to protect it.
stories.headline: Barcelona retailers and city hall clash over proposed commercial-rent regulation
